name: Vespid Dynamics
employees: 61,000 direct; estimated 400,000 autonomous units under management
sovereign_territory: Vespid Arcology Cluster, eastern Gary Sprawl, Indiana Corridor — a network of seven interlocked hive-architecture towers connected by enclosed drone transit tubes, collectively called the Comb
founding_story: Founded in 2141 by entomologist-turned-engineer Dr. Sable Mroz and logistics mogul Canto Ferreira, Vespid Dynamics emerged from a DARPA-adjacent research program studying eusocial insect behavior as a model for autonomous fleet coordination. When the federal government collapsed its drone infrastructure contracts in 2144, Mroz and Ferreira spun the research out privately and relocated to the Gary Sprawl, where land was cheap and airspace regulation was essentially nonexistent. Their first commercial product, the VSD-7 'Worker' delivery drone, became the backbone of last-mile logistics across the GLMZ corridor within three years. The company's swarm-intelligence software — branded HEXCORE — proved so effective at coordinating thousands of units simultaneously that it was quietly re-licensed to three Big 20 defense contractors before Vespid had reached its fifth birthday. The founders never forgot the government's betrayal of the original program; Vespid declared sovereign corponation status in 2149 and has maintained a pointed hostility toward municipal airspace authorities ever since.
security_force: The Lancers — a 3,200-strong paramilitary unit equipped with Vespid's own Hornet-class combat drones and light infantry. Lancers specialize in aerial denial operations and are among the most effective anti-drone forces in the corridor, using swarm-vs-swarm tactics developed in-house. Ground personnel are supported by Sentinel-class autonomous sentinels that patrol the Comb's perimeter in rotating formations. The Lancers have been contracted out for three documented corporate conflicts in the past decade.
key_detail: Vespid's HEXCORE swarm AI operates on a genuinely decentralized architecture — there is no single node that controls the fleet. This makes it nearly impossible to shut down via conventional cyberattack, but has also led to several documented incidents of drone swarms exhibiting emergent behaviors their operators did not program. The most serious of these, the 2158 'Murmuration Event,' saw a fleet of 12,000 Worker drones spontaneously reroute themselves into a holding pattern over Lake Michigan for 11 hours before resuming normal operations. Vespid's official explanation cited a 'harmonic resonance in route-optimization subroutines.' Nobody believed them.
relationship_to_big_20: Not a member of the Big 20. Vespid holds significant leverage over the group, however, because an estimated 34% of Big 20 logistics operations rely on Vespid drone infrastructure in some capacity. Kelpline Logistics and Stonepath Logistics both pay substantial licensing fees for HEXCORE integration. Carrion Defense Works has a standing rivalry over swarm-defense contracts. Vespid is frequently nominated for Big 20 membership and repeatedly declines, preferring the flexibility of independent status.
full_text: Vespid Dynamics Autonomous Systems Corponation — stock designation VSD, commonly called The Hive or Yellow-and-Black — is a Φ312 billion swarm logistics and autonomous defense corponation headquartered in the Vespid Arcology Cluster on the eastern edge of the Gary Sprawl. The company was founded in 2141 by Dr. Sable Mroz and Canto Ferreira from the ruins of a collapsed federal drone research program, relocating to Indiana Corridor airspace where regulatory friction was minimal. Their HEXCORE swarm-intelligence platform, modeled on eusocial insect coordination, became the dominant autonomous fleet management system in the GLMZ corridor and has since been licensed to defense and logistics operations across North America. Vespid declared corponation sovereignty in 2149 and operates from the Comb, a seven-tower arcology network connected by enclosed drone transit tubes. The company's 61,000 direct employees manage an estimated 400,000 autonomous units at any given time, with revenue of Φ48.7 billion annually. Security is handled by the Lancers, a 3,200-strong paramilitary force specializing in aerial denial and swarm-versus-swarm combat. HEXCORE's fully decentralized architecture is both its greatest strength and its most troubling characteristic — the 2158 Murmuration Event, in which 12,000 drones held an unexplained formation over Lake Michigan for eleven hours, remains officially unexplained. Vespid is not a Big 20 member and declines all nominations, though roughly a third of Big 20 logistics operations depend on its infrastructure.

glmzTerritory.description: Vespid Arcology Cluster — network of hardened research and manufacturing facilities in the eastern Gary Sprawl and Zone 11 Indiana Corridor. Aerospace and autonomous systems; positioned as a lower-profile Arcturus competitor. Zone 6-11 positioning keeps Vespid outside Zone 2's Arcturus Civil Security monitoring range.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: Vespid facilities are heavily hardened. Gray Zone communities in the adjacent Indiana corridor are aware of where the perimeter is.
